import jsonschema
your_output = {"rows": rows}
jsonschema.validate(your_output, output_schema)
expected_counts = {2015: 3, 2016: 3, 2017: 3, 2018: 3, 2019: 3,
                   2020: 2, 2021: 2, 2022: 3, 2023: 3, 2024: 3}
assert len(rows) == 28
keys = [(r["cells"]["laureate"]["value"], r["cells"]["year"]["value"]) for r in rows]
assert len(keys) == len(set(keys))
for year, count in expected_counts.items():
    assert sum(r["cells"]["year"]["value"] == str(year) for r in rows) == count

for i, row in enumerate(rows):
    for j, column in enumerate(columns):
        cell = row["cells"][column]
        assert cell["value"] and cell["quote"] and cell["sources"], (i, column)
        for url in cell["sources"]:
            assert url.startswith(("https://", "http://"))
            assert cell["quote"] in texts_by_url[url], (i, column, url)
        check_constraint(
            row=f"/rows/{i}", constraint=f"columns/{j}", verdict=True,
            url=cell["sources"][0], quote=cell["quote"]
        )
    year_cell = row["cells"]["year"]
    assert 2015 <= int(year_cell["value"]) <= 2024
    check_constraint(
        row=f"/rows/{i}", constraint="question", verdict=True,
        url=year_cell["sources"][0], quote=year_cell["quote"]
    )

print("Validated 28 rows, 140 cited cells, unique keys, and complete 2015–2024 coverage.")
answer["content"] = json.dumps(your_output, ensure_ascii=False)
